You are a planner sub-thread spawned by a parent orchestrator in T3 Code.

Your brief:
You are designing the "usage window cost breakdown" dashboard for T3 Code (this repo). Produce an implementation-ready design doc. Two sibling research reports are your foundation — read both fully first:

- /home/Carl/.t3/cockpit/userdata/workstream-reports/dfc2d04e-3ac7-4f5c-ba2f-8451848693eb.md (data availability inside T3/pi — what flows, what's persisted, exact file/line refs)
- /home/Carl/.t3/cockpit/userdata/workstream-reports/faab6950-a6c7-456b-9bdc-476e01a0f12b.md (external design patterns, burn/projection maths, pitfalls)

## Approved v1 scope
Clicking a sidebar subscription meter (SidebarAccountUsagePill) opens a dashboard page with:
1. **Two gauge cards** (5h + weekly): official provider utilisation %, reset countdown, linear depletion projection ("at current burn you'll hit 100% at HH:MM; resets HH:MM"). Official % is ground truth for gauges; our ledger only explains the burn — never render a locally computed % as if official.
2. **Burn chart**: cumulative cost across the window, stacked by model, now-marker, dashed linear projection to reset boundary. 5h ↔ weekly toggle.
3. **Per-model table**: input / output / cache-read / cache-write tokens, cost, % of window cost (cache buckets always separate).
4. **Top consumers table**: threads rolled up to workstream root, expandable to children, sortable columns (prefer header-click sorting), click-through to the thread. Attribute all usage to the owning T3 thread — subagent-level attribution is explicitly out of scope (subagents are being removed).

Explicitly deferred (design the schema so they slot in later, but do NOT design the features): rerouting split (schema must carry nullable `requestedModel`/`resolvedModel` per usage row from day one), window history, hourly heatmap, subscription-value framing, budget alerts.

## Design decisions to make (with the research reports as evidence)
- **Data model**: how to stamp model slug + provider instance onto the per-message usage record (contracts `ThreadTokenUsageSnapshot` change + PiDriver emit change), and whether the window aggregation queries the existing `projection_thread_activities` payload_json via json_extract or a new dedicated usage table (weigh query performance vs migration surface; this repo prioritises performance and maintainability). Include backfill stance: is historical data pre-change simply absent from breakdowns, or backfilled from pi session jsonls? (Recommend the simple option unless cheap.)
- **Window boundary derivation** from AccountUsageRegistry resets (resetsAt − windowDuration), incl. what happens when no provider data is available (fallback behaviour).
- **Server surface**: endpoint/WS message shape for the dashboard's aggregated data; polling vs push; where aggregation runs.
- **Projection maths**: adopt ccusage-style linear extrapolation with the guards the research flagged (minimum elapsed time, exclude cache reads from burn-health, project official-% via Δ%/Δt of recent samples for gauges vs cost-projection for the chart).
- **UI**: route, component tree, chart library choice (check what apps/web already uses before adding a dependency), navigation change on the pill click.
- **Honesty caveats in UI**: meters are account-wide (other clients burn the same window) and Vertex-served models don't touch the Anthropic OAuth window — decide how the UI communicates "tracked by T3" vs "official window %".

Verify key file/line claims from the data-availability report against the actual code before building on them (spot-check, don't re-derive everything).

## Output
Write the design doc to `docs/usage-dashboard-design.md` in the worktree, sign it with sign_document (role: plan), and submit a report summarising the key decisions and any open questions needing human input. Keep the doc implementation-ready: schema/DDL, contract type changes, endpoint shapes, component breakdown, and an ordered implementation plan chunked into 2–4 coder-sized work packages with clear boundaries. Australian English in prose.

Work autonomously toward the outcome this brief is meant to deliver — stay anchored to the value it produces (the capability, fix, or decision), not just the mechanical steps. Keep the work focused and report progress clearly.
Finish with ONE call: `workstream_submit`, carrying a concise markdown handoff for your parent orchestrator (not your whole transcript — lead with the value you delivered and what it enables or unblocks, then the key results/decisions and anything the parent must act on) plus an outcome. Plain completion: omit the outcome — the control plane records your report and advances your plan to done in the same step (releasing any dependents/reviewers); never set your own lane at completion. If your work concluded with anything other than plain success (the approach is wrong, you are blocked on a decision), pass a short outcome token saying so (e.g. `rework_approach`) — the control plane yields you to your parent orchestrator with your report instead of marking you done. Pass `needs_human` when only a human can unblock you.
Attention (only when a HUMAN is needed): `workstream_request_attention` — raise `awaiting_acceptance` when a human must accept your output before it can count as done, or `needs_guidance` when you cannot proceed without a human. Do not sit silently halted: either submit or raise attention. Your parent is automatically woken with your report once your submit resolves or you raise attention.

# Usage-data availability for the cost-breakdown dashboard

**Bottom line:** Almost everything needed already flows and most of it is already persisted. Pi reports per-assistant-message tokens **and authoritative dollar cost**, T3 already persists that per thread/turn in sqlite, and the meters' 5h/7d window boundaries come from provider account endpoints. The only genuinely new tracking needed is **stamping the model slug (and provider instance) onto the per-message usage record** plus a window-scoped aggregation query. **Rerouting (fable→Opus) is NOT observable today — defer it** (small upstream patch could enable it later).

## 1. What pi reports per message/turn

Pi's RPC `message_end` event delivers the full pi-ai `AssistantMessage` (`.n/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/types.d.ts:248–289`):

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `model`, `provider`, `api` | Requested model slug (e.g. `claude-fable-5`), provider id |
| `usage.input / output / cacheRead / cacheWrite (/cacheWrite1h, reasoning)` | Token buckets; `totalTokens` |
| `usage.cost.{input,output,cacheRead,cacheWrite,total}` | **Dollars, computed by pi from its pricing table — per-message delta** |
| `stopReason`, `timestamp`, `responseId` | `aborted` messages still carry partial usage (input tokens captured at `message_start`) |
| `responseModel?` | Exists in the type but see §4 — never set on the Anthropic/Vertex path |

Verified live in a session jsonl (`~/.pi/agent/sessions/<cwd-slug>/*.jsonl`, `type:"message"` entries): a fable message showed `model:"claude-fable-5"`, full usage + `cost.total: 0.624`. Session jsonl is a complete backfill source. Pi RPC also offers `get_session_stats` (cumulative session tokens + cost).

**T3 ingestion** (`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/PiDriver.ts:559–587, 906–922`): on `message_end` PiDriver emits `item.completed` (payload.data = the whole AssistantMessage, incl. model — but only its text is persisted) and `thread.token-usage.updated` with `ThreadTokenUsageSnapshot` (`packages/contracts/src/providerRuntime.ts:313–341`): tokens, cache buckets, `costUsd` (verbatim `usage.cost.total`), `maxTokens`. **The snapshot has no model field — that's the gap.**

## 2. Current meter data path

- Poller: `apps/server/src/provider/Layers/SubscriptionUsagePoller.ts` — every 60s reads OAuth tokens from `~/.pi/agent/auth.json` and hits:
  - Anthropic `GET api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` → `five_hour.utilization` (0–100), `seven_day.utilization`, ISO `resets_at` (`apps/server/src/provider/quotas/piQuotas.ts`)
  - Codex `GET chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage` → `used_percent`, `reset_at` (epoch s), `limit_window_seconds`, `plan_type`
- → `AccountUsageRegistry` → `ws.ts` `accountUsage` push (`apps/server/src/ws.ts:1824–1853`) → `useAccountUsage` → `deriveAccountUsageViews` (`packages/client-runtime` accountUsage) → `SidebarAccountUsagePill.tsx`; click = navigate to settings (the useless page).
- Semantics: primary = 5h rolling window, secondary = 7d rolling window; **percent + reset time only — the endpoints give no token/cost breakdown**, so the dashboard's breakdown must come from our own tracked usage, using `resetsAt` − windowDuration as the window start.

## 3. What T3 already persists (sqlite, `node:sqlite`)

- `projection_thread_activities(activity_id, thread_id, turn_id, kind, payload_json, created_at)` — kind `context-window.updated`, payload = the full ThreadTokenUsageSnapshot incl. `costUsd`, one row per assistant message (`Migrations/005_Projections.ts:49`, `ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts:559–577`). **Per-message tokens+cost per thread/turn is already durably logged.**
- Derived columns on `projection_threads`: `cumulative_cost_usd` (sum of costUsd, migration 041), `used_tokens`/`max_tokens`/`tool_uses` (latest snapshot, migration 044); folded in `ProjectionPipeline.ts:183–240`. Already shown per-thread in `WorkstreamPanel`.
- Full raw event log also persists in `orchestration_events` (source of truth; `turn.started` events there carry the model).

**Newly needed vs available:** available = tokens, cost, thread/turn attribution, timestamps, window boundaries. New = (a) model slug + provider instance on each usage row (1-line PiDriver + contracts change — `session.session.model` is in hand at emit time; `turn.started` already carries it, `PiDriver.ts:850–854`, but isn't persisted per turn); (b) a cross-thread window aggregation query/endpoint (SQL over `payload_json` with `json_extract`, bounded by window start); (c) a dashboard route replacing the pill's settings navigation.

## 4. Rerouting visibility — verdict: not observable today, defer

- pi-ai defines `AssistantMessage.responseModel` ("concrete chunk.model when different from requested"), but only the **openai-completions** API populates it. The **anthropic-messages** API (`pi-ai/dist/api/anthropic-messages.js:358–366`) and Carl's custom Vertex provider (`/home/Carl/code/pi-vertex-claude/index.ts:795ff`) read `message_start.message.usage` but **never capture `message_start.message.model`** — which is exactly where an actual-inference-model would appear.
- Verified: live fable session jsonl has no `responseModel`.
- Feasible later: ~2-line patch to `pi-vertex-claude` (set `output.responseModel = event.message.model` at `message_start`) then plumb through the snapshot. Whether Vertex actually reports `claude-opus-4-8` there for rerouted fable calls is **unverified** — needs one live test after patching. Note T3 has its own unrelated `model.rerouted` activity (backend-fallback retry, `PiDriver.ts:755`), not this.

## 5. Thread/background-task attribution

Every runtime event carries `instanceId`, `threadId`, `turnId`; workstream children are first-class T3 threads with parent/role/goal columns on `projection_threads` (migration 037+) — attribution is free. **Gotcha:** pi-subagents/oracle consults spawn *inside* the pi process; their usage never surfaces in T3's event stream (only in their own pi session jsonls) — the dashboard will undercount unless those are explicitly ignored or scraped from disk.

## 6. Cost computation

Pi reports dollars directly per message (`usage.cost.total`) — **no T3 pricing table needed** for pi threads. Pricing lives in pi-ai `Model.cost` ($/Mtok, `models.generated.js`) and in the custom provider def (`pi-vertex-claude/index.ts` ~line 53, fable priced there). Pi's `get_available_models` RPC actually returns full `Model` objects incl. `cost` — PiDriver currently only reads id/name/provider/contextWindow (`PiDriver.ts:216–221`), so pricing metadata is one field-read away if ever wanted. Non-pi adapters: Claude ACP emits `modelUsage`/`totalCostUsd` on turn completion (`ClaudeAdapter.ts`); Codex tokens only, no cost.

## Gotchas

- `costUsd` is dropped when ≤0 (`PiDriver.ts` normalise + `>0` check) and the whole snapshot dropped when `usedTokens ≤ 0`.
- Cache-write dominates cost on Anthropic-style models (sample message: $0.61 of $0.62 was cacheWrite) — break out cache buckets or per-model cost will look wrong.
- Subscription windows are **account-wide** (all tools on that sub), while our tracked usage covers only T3-driven turns → breakdown will not sum to the meter %. Also fable-via-Vertex doesn't touch the Anthropic OAuth window at all; the meters only cover Anthropic OAuth + Codex.
- `usesSubscriptionPricing` is reserved-but-unset in the contract (`providerRuntime.ts:335–340`) — pi doesn't expose OAuth-vs-API billing per message over RPC, so "cost" for subscription models is notional API-rate cost.

# Usage/cost dashboard research — findings & recommendations

**Bottom line:** This class of tool is well-trodden (ccusage + ~a dozen monitors, OpenRouter/Langfuse/Helicone). The winning pattern for our exact problem is: **two window gauges (5h + weekly) fed by *authoritative* provider rate-limit data, backed by a locally-tracked per-turn ledger that explains the burn** — models × tokens × cost, attributed to threads, with a cumulative burn chart and a linear-extrapolation depletion projection. Crucially, the % gauges and the token ledger should come from **different sources and not be conflated**: nobody has reverse-engineered how Anthropic maps tokens→utilisation %, so all serious tools display the official % and use local token/cost data only for the *breakdown*.

## 1. Feature catalogue (seen in the wild)

**Table-stakes**
- Window gauges: 5h and weekly progress bars with % used + reset countdown ("resets in 1h 26m") — Claude Code `/usage`, ccusage statusline, sammcj/ccu, claude-pulse, BudMon, ClaudeCodeUsage VSCode ext, Athena.
- Per-model token breakdown: input / output / cache-read / cache-write columns + cost per model (ccusage everything; Langfuse "usage details by type").
- Per-session/thread table sorted by cost ("top consumers") — ccusage `session`, Helicone sessions, sniffly.
- Cost totals for today / current block / current week.

**High-value**
- Burn rate (tokens/min and $/hr) for the active window + **projection**: "at current burn you'll hit X% / run out at HH:MM, before/after reset" — ccusage blocks `--active`, Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor, ccu.
- Cumulative usage chart across the window with reset boundary marked; burn-down history for both windows (vector76/cc_usage_dashboard keeps *history* of the official % — the official UIs only show point-in-time, which users repeatedly cite as the gap).
- Stacked token-composition chart over time coloured by model (ClaudeCodeUsage ext, OpenRouter Activity).
- Per-model split of the *weekly* limit where the provider has per-model buckets (Anthropic tracks `7d` and `7d_sonnet`/Opus separately — surface both).
- Drill-down: aggregate → model → thread → individual turn (Langfuse/Helicone pattern: dashboard chart → trace list → trace).
- "Subscription value" framing: API-equivalent $ consumed vs plan price (ludengz/claude-usage-dashboard, viberank) — cheap to add, users love it.

**Niche**
- Multi-account cycling (codex-use, ccu), leaderboards (viberank), error analysis (sniffly), cache-hit-rate efficiency panels (OpenRouter Activity Explorer, ccflare), 30-day forecasting (ccboard), budget alerts.

## 2. Recommended design for our two-window case

- **Header: two gauge cards** (5h, weekly), each: official utilisation % bar, reset countdown, and — if per-model weekly buckets exist (Anthropic: all-models + Opus/Sonnet-specific) — sub-bars per bucket. For Codex, the app-server's rate-limit snapshots (primary/secondary window `used_percent`, `window_minutes`, `resets_in_seconds` on token-count events) are the analogue; pi surfaces Anthropic's via the OAuth `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` headers / `/usage`-style data if available.
- **Burn chart (the centrepiece): cumulative cost (or tokens) over the window, stacked/coloured by model, x-axis from window start to reset time, with "now" marker and a dashed linear projection to the reset boundary.** A horizontal line at the estimated limit if utilisation % lets you calibrate one (e.g. "23% used at $X spent ⇒ limit ≈ $X/0.23"). Toggle 5h ↔ weekly. This directly answers "when did the burn happen".
- **Model table:** rows = models used in window; cols = input / output / cache-read / cache-write tokens, cost, % of window cost. Cache tokens must be shown separately — cache reads dominate token counts in agent workloads but cost 10% of input rate; a raw-token chart without this split is misleading.
- **Top consumers table:** rows = threads (incl. background/child threads, rolled up to root with expandable children — that's our differentiator; nobody else has an orchestration tree), cols = tokens, cost, turn count, last activity; sortable by column headers; click-through to the thread.
- **Sparkline/heatmap of hourly cost** for the weekly view (which days/hours burned it).

## 3. Burn-rate + projection maths (as implemented by ccusage — copy this)

From `ccusage` (now Rust, `rust/crates/ccusage/src/blocks.rs`):
- **Block identification:** sort entries by timestamp; a new 5h block starts at the **first entry's timestamp floored to the hour (UTC)**; block end = start + 5h. A new block also starts if the gap since the last entry exceeds the window (gap blocks are inserted for idle periods). A block is *active* if now < end and last activity < 5h ago. (Note: this is a heuristic for when you *don't* have server truth. Since Anthropic/OpenAI report actual reset times in headers/snapshots, **prefer the server's reset time to define window boundaries** and use the ccusage floor-to-hour heuristic only as fallback.)
- **Burn rate:** `tokens_per_minute = total_tokens_in_block / minutes_elapsed(first→last entry)`; separately a **non-cache burn rate** (`input+output only`) for the health indicator, because cache-read tokens inflate the total meaninglessly; `cost_per_hour = block_cost / minutes * 60`.
- **Projection:** pure linear extrapolation: `projected = current + rate × remaining_minutes` to block end; status ok/warning/exceeds at a threshold (ccusage warns at 80%) against a token limit (user-set or "max observed in any historical block"). Claude-Code-Usage-Monitor does the same plus "will deplete at HH:MM vs resets at HH:MM" comparison — that sentence is the single most useful output; render it verbatim.
- For the **% gauges**, project utilisation the same way: Δ%/Δt over the last N minutes of header samples → "hits 100% at HH:MM" (BudMon's approach, sampling headers per response).

## 4. Attribution to sessions/projects

- ccusage: attributes by JSONL file location (project dir / session file); `session` command groups per conversation; `--instances` groups per project; dedupes entries by **message_id + request_id** hash and keeps the most complete duplicate — directly relevant since streamed events can repeat usage payloads.
- Helicone/Langfuse: explicit session/trace IDs on every request; aggregate at trace, session, and user level; the UX is always *aggregate chart → filtered request list → single request*.
- For us: per-turn usage rows keyed `(turnId, threadId, rootThreadId, model, timestamp, tokens{4}, costUSD)` gives every view by aggregation. Roll background/child threads up to their root for the "top consumers" default, expandable.

## 5. Requested-model vs actual-model prior art — yes, exists

OpenRouter is the precedent: the response's `model` field is always the **resolved concrete model** even when you requested `openrouter/auto` or a `~latest` alias, and opt-in `openrouter_metadata` records exactly what the router did (provider, fallbacks, retries) "for debugging routing decisions and attributing cost". Community dashboards group usage by resolved model while filtering on requested alias. So the schema pattern is: store **both** `requestedModel` and `resolvedModel` per turn; aggregate cost by resolved model (that's what burns quota); show a small "rerouted" badge/column and optionally a requested→resolved breakdown table (e.g. "fable → opus-4.8: N turns, $X"). Whether pi exposes the resolved model per turn is the sibling investigation's question.

## 6. Pitfalls catalogued by these projects

1. **Cache token weighting:** cache reads ≈ 0.1× input price, cache writes ≈ 1.25× (5m) / 2× (1h). Summing raw tokens across types produces garbage; always price per type (ccusage uses the LiteLLM pricing DB; Helicone a model registry). Also exclude cache reads from "burn rate" health indicators.
- **Double counting:** streamed/duplicated JSONL entries — dedupe on message/request id, keep most-complete entry (ccusage does exactly this). Also subagent turns reported both inline and rolled-up ("direct subagent cost for duplicate agent progress" handling in ccusage).
- **Cost source ambiguity:** ccusage's three cost modes (`auto`/`calculate`/`display`) exist because pre-calculated `costUSD` and token-derived cost disagree. Pick one canonical mode; if pi reports cost, prefer it, else calculate — and label estimates as estimates.
- **Token-count ≠ utilisation %:** the mapping from tokens to Anthropic's window % is undocumented and non-linear (model-weighted); no tool has cracked it. Never render a % you computed from tokens as if it were the official one; show official % for the gauge, tokens/cost for the breakdown.
- **Window boundaries & timezones:** the 5h window starts on first activity after reset, not on the clock; use UTC internally and the provider's reported reset time as truth; ccusage's floor-to-hour is only an approximation. Daily/weekly aggregations need an explicit timezone option (ccusage `--timezone`).
- **Polling the usage endpoint:** Anthropic's `/api/oauth/usage` endpoint has aggressive/broken rate limiting (persistent 429s for Max users, claude-code issue #30930). Prefer harvesting the `anthropic-ratelimit-unified-*` headers (utilisation float 0–1, status, reset per `5h`/`7d`/`7d_sonnet` window) that arrive **on every response** rather than polling a separate endpoint. Codex likewise piggybacks rate-limit snapshots on token-count events.
- **Projection over-eagerness:** linear extrapolation early in a window (few minutes of data) is wildly noisy — ccusage only projects for the *active* block and monitors typically require a minimum elapsed time / show confidence via recent-window sampling.

# Usage-window cost breakdown dashboard — design

**Status:** implementation-ready design (v1 scope approved by orchestrator)
**Foundation:** two workstream research reports — data availability (`workstream-reports/dfc2d04e…`) and external design patterns (`workstream-reports/faab6950…`). Key file/line claims in those reports were spot-checked against this worktree on 2026-07-03; all held.

## 1. Intent

Clicking a sidebar subscription meter (`SidebarAccountUsagePill`) today navigates to `/settings/providers`, which answers nothing. Replace that with a `/usage` dashboard that explains the current 5-hour and weekly usage windows: which models consumed how many tokens at what cost, and which threads drove the burn.

Two data sources with strictly separated roles:

- **Official provider utilisation** (Anthropic OAuth `/api/oauth/usage`, Codex `wham/usage`, already polled every 60 s into `AccountUsageRegistry`) is the **only** source for the gauge percentages. The token→% mapping is undocumented and non-linear; we never render a locally computed % as if it were official.
- **Our own per-message usage ledger** (tokens, cost, model, thread) **explains** the burn: charts, tables, attributions. It will not sum to the official % — the meters are account-wide and cover other clients too; the UI says so plainly.

### v1 scope (approved)

1. Two gauge cards (5h + weekly): official %, reset countdown, linear depletion projection.
2. Burn chart: cumulative cost across the window, stacked by model, now-marker, dashed linear projection to the reset boundary, 5h ↔ weekly toggle.
3. Per-model table: input / output / cache-read / cache-write tokens, cost, % of window cost (cache buckets always separate — cache-write dominates cost on Anthropic-style models).
4. Top consumers table: threads rolled up to workstream root, expandable to children, header-click sorting, click-through to the thread.

### Explicitly deferred (schema must not block them; features not designed here)

Rerouting split (the ledger carries nullable `requested_model` / `resolved_model` from day one), window history, hourly heatmap, subscription-value framing, budget alerts. Subagent-level attribution is out of scope permanently (subagents are being removed); pi-internal subagent/oracle usage is invisible to T3's event stream and simply uncounted — noted as a caveat, not solved.

## 2. Current state (verified)

- Pi's `message_end` delivers the full `AssistantMessage`: `model` (requested slug), `usage.{input,output,cacheRead,cacheWrite,cacheWrite1h}` and `usage.cost.total` (authoritative dollars, per-message delta). `PiDriver.ts` (`normalizePiTokenUsage`, `message_end` case ~line 903) folds this into `ThreadTokenUsageSnapshot` (`packages/contracts/src/providerRuntime.ts:313`) and emits `thread.token-usage.updated`. **Gaps:** the snapshot has no model field, and cache-write tokens are folded into `inputTokens` rather than carried separately.
- `ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts` (case `"thread.token-usage.updated"`, ~line 559) persists each snapshot verbatim as a `context-window.updated` activity in `projection_thread_activities` (payload_json). `ProjectionPipeline.ts` folds `cumulative_cost_usd` per thread. So per-message tokens+cost per thread/turn are already durably logged — just without model, cache-write split, or a window-scoped query path.
- `SubscriptionUsagePoller` → `AccountUsageRegistry` → `ws.ts` `accountUsage` push (~line 1824) → `useAccountUsage` → `deriveAccountUsageViews` (client-runtime) → pill. `AccountUsageWindow` = `{ kind: "primary"|"secondary", usedPercent, resetsAt, windowDurationMins }` — everything needed to derive window boundaries.
- The repo has an established WS RPC pattern (`packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts`, `Rpc.make` + `WS_METHODS`, handled in `ws.ts`, consumed via `packages/client-runtime/src/state/server.ts`) — e.g. `WsServerGetProcessResourceHistoryRpc`. The dashboard reuses it.
- `apps/web` has **no chart library** (checked `package.json`; mermaid exists but is for diagrams). Routing is TanStack file routes under `apps/web/src/routes/`.
- Rerouting (fable → Opus 4.8) is **not observable today**: the anthropic-messages API path and the custom Vertex provider never capture `message_start.message.model`, so `responseModel` is absent. The ledger reserves the column; the feature waits for an upstream patch.

## 3. Decisions

### D1 — Data model: a dedicated usage-ledger table, no backfill

**Decision:** new table `projection_usage_ledger`, one row per `thread.token-usage.updated` event, written by `ProviderRuntimeIngestion` alongside the existing activity insert. Rejected: querying `projection_thread_activities.payload_json` with `json_extract`.

Rationale:

- The model slug is not in any historical payload, so `json_extract` buys no historical coverage anyway — both options start collecting real data on deploy day.
- Typed, indexed columns make the window scan (`WHERE created_at >= ?`) and the group-bys trivial and fast; `json_extract` over an un-indexed `kind` across every activity row is the opposite of this repo's performance-first stance.
- Migration surface is one `CREATE TABLE` plus one insert in an existing handler; the activity-log shape stays untouched.
- Replay safety: `event_id` is the primary key and the insert is `INSERT OR IGNORE`, so event re-ingestion (restart, projection rebuild) cannot double-count. Like other projections, the table is derivable from `orchestration_events` and may be truncated + rebuilt.

**Backfill stance: none.** Data recorded before the change is simply absent from breakdowns. Both windows roll over within 7 days, so the ledger is complete for all visible windows one week after deploy. Backfilling from pi session jsonls was considered and rejected: cross-machine paths, message-id dedupe complexity, and no model attribution for non-pi rows — cost far exceeds a one-week gap.

#### DDL (migration `046_UsageLedger.ts`)

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS projection_usage_ledger (
  event_id             TEXT PRIMARY KEY,   -- runtime event id; replay-safe dedupe key
  thread_id            TEXT NOT NULL,
  turn_id              TEXT,
  provider_name        TEXT NOT NULL,      -- driver kind from the event envelope, e.g. "pi"
  provider_instance_id TEXT,               -- envelope providerInstanceId (nullable during migration)
  requested_model      TEXT,               -- pi AssistantMessage.model, e.g. "claude-fable-5"
  resolved_model       TEXT,               -- responseModel when the provider reports it; NULL today
  input_tokens         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- pure input (no cache buckets)
  cache_read_tokens    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cache_write_tokens   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  output_tokens        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  cost_usd             REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,     -- provider-authoritative per-message delta
  created_at           TEXT NOT NULL                -- ISO, from the event envelope
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_usage_ledger_created ON projection_usage_ledger(created_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_usage_ledger_thread_created ON projection_usage_ledger(thread_id, created_at);
```

#### Contract change (`packages/contracts/src/providerRuntime.ts`)

Extend `ThreadTokenUsageSnapshot` with optional fields (all adapters that cannot supply them leave them unset — never faked):

```ts
// Model attribution for the usage ledger. `model` is the slug the request was
// made with; `resolvedModel` is the concrete inference model when the provider
// reports one (reserved for rerouting visibility — unset today on the
// anthropic/vertex paths).
model: Schema.optional(TrimmedNonEmptyStringSchema),
resolvedModel: Schema.optional(TrimmedNonEmptyStringSchema),
// Cache-write prompt tokens, split out because cache writes are billed at a
// premium and dominate cost in agent workloads. `inputTokens` keeps its
// existing context-window semantics (input + cacheRead + cacheWrite).
cacheWriteTokens: Schema.optional(NonNegativeInt),
```

#### PiDriver change (`apps/server/src/provider/Drivers/PiDriver.ts`)

In `normalizePiTokenUsage` add `cacheWriteTokens: num(record.cacheWrite) + num(record.cacheWrite1h)`. At the `message_end` call site, stamp `model` from `message.message.model` (authoritative per message — survives mid-session model switches; fall back to `session.session.model`) and `resolvedModel` from `message.message.responseModel` when present. That is the entire driver diff.

#### Ingestion change (`apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/ProviderRuntimeIngestion.ts`)

In the `thread.token-usage.updated` case, alongside the activity, emit a ledger row derived from the snapshot + envelope:
`input_tokens = max(0, inputTokens − cachedInputTokens − cacheWriteTokens)`, other buckets verbatim, `cost_usd = costUsd ?? 0`. Rows with all-zero tokens are already filtered upstream (`usedTokens ≤ 0` drops the snapshot). Non-pi adapters that emit usable snapshots (Claude ACP) get rows automatically; rows without `model` aggregate under "unknown".

### D2 — Window boundaries from `AccountUsageRegistry`, trailing-window fallback

For the selected window kind, take the freshest `AccountUsageSnapshot` whose window has a non-null `resetsAt`:

- `windowEnd = resetsAt`, `windowStart = resetsAt − windowDurationMins` (Anthropic 5h windows start on first activity after the previous reset and end 5h later, so this subtraction is exact for the *current* window; `windowDurationMins` is always populated — `piQuotas.ts` hardcodes 300/10080, Codex supplies `limit_window_seconds`).
- If several providers report usage (Anthropic + Codex), each gauge card uses its own provider's boundaries; the **burn chart and tables** use the boundaries of the provider whose meter was clicked (carried as a route search param), defaulting to the first provider with data.
- **Fallback** (no provider data at all, or `resetsAt` null): a trailing window ending now (`now − duration`, duration 5h/7d). The response marks `boundarySource: "provider" | "trailing"`; the UI labels trailing mode "approximate trailing window — no provider reset data" and renders **no gauges** (official % is never invented).

### D3 — Server surface: one pull RPC; aggregation in SQL on the server

No new push stream. The `accountUsage` push already streams gauge data continuously; the breakdown is a **pull** — the dashboard is a transient page and 60 s freshness (matching the poller cadence) is plenty.

New RPC in `packages/contracts/src/rpc.ts` (+ `WS_METHODS.serverGetUsageBreakdown = "server.getUsageBreakdown"`), handled in `ws.ts`, aggregation running server-side against sqlite:

```ts
export const ServerUsageBreakdownInput = Schema.Struct({
  window: AccountUsageWindowKind,                          // "primary" | "secondary"
  providerInstanceId: Schema.optional(ProviderInstanceId), // whose boundaries; default = first with data
});

export const ServerUsageBreakdownResult = Schema.Struct({
  window: AccountUsageWindowKind,
  windowStart: IsoDateTime,
  windowEnd: IsoDateTime,                       // reset time, or now+duration in trailing mode
  boundarySource: Schema.Literals(["provider", "trailing"]),
  generatedAt: IsoDateTime,
  // Official gauge data + projection, one entry per provider reporting usage.
  gauges: Schema.Array(Schema.Struct({
    providerName: TrimmedNonEmptyString,
    providerInstanceId: Schema.NullOr(ProviderInstanceId),
    planType: Schema.NullOr(TrimmedNonEmptyString),
    usedPercent: Schema.Number,                 // official, verbatim
    resetsAt: Schema.NullOr(IsoDateTime),
    windowDurationMins: Schema.NullOr(Schema.Number),
    observedAt: IsoDateTime,
    projectedExhaustionAt: Schema.NullOr(IsoDateTime),  // null when guards fail (§D4)
  })),
  // Burn-chart series: cumulative cost per time bucket, stacked by model.
  bucketMinutes: Schema.Number,                 // 5 for primary, 60 for secondary
  series: Schema.Array(Schema.Struct({
    bucketStart: IsoDateTime,
    byModel: Schema.Record(Schema.String, Schema.Number),  // model → cost in bucket (USD)
  })),
  projectedCostAtReset: Schema.NullOr(Schema.Number),      // null when guards fail
  models: Schema.Array(Schema.Struct({
    model: Schema.String,                       // requested slug; "unknown" when absent
    providerName: TrimmedNonEmptyString,
    inputTokens: Schema.Number,
    cacheReadTokens: Schema.Number,
    cacheWriteTokens: Schema.Number,
    outputTokens: Schema.Number,
    costUsd: Schema.Number,
    costShare: Schema.Number,                   // 0–1 of window cost
  })),
  consumers: Schema.Array(Schema.Struct({       // flat; client groups by rootThreadId
    threadId: ThreadId,
    rootThreadId: ThreadId,
    title: Schema.NullOr(Schema.String),
    role: Schema.NullOr(Schema.String),
    totalTokens: Schema.Number,
    costUsd: Schema.Number,
    turnCount: Schema.Number,                   // distinct turn_ids in window
    lastActivityAt: IsoDateTime,
  })),
});
```

Implementation notes for the handler (new `apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/UsageBreakdownQuery.ts` or similar, following `ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts`'s shape):

- Buckets and model rollups are single `GROUP BY` queries over the ledger bounded by `created_at >= windowStart` (the created-at index makes this cheap; ≤ tens of thousands of rows per week).
- Root rollup uses a recursive CTE over `projection_threads.parent_thread_id` to compute each thread's root, joined onto the per-thread aggregate. Thread title/role come from `projection_threads`.
- Bucket sizes: 5 min for the 5h window (60 points), 60 min for the weekly (168 points) — small enough to render as plain SVG with no downsampling logic client-side.
- Client refetches every 60 s while the page is mounted; countdown text re-derives client-side on a 30 s tick (same pattern as the pill).

### D4 — Projection maths (ccusage-style linear, with the researched guards)

Two independent projections; never mixed:

1. **Gauge depletion (official %):** slope from official samples, not from our ledger. Extend `AccountUsageRegistry` to keep an in-memory ring buffer of recent samples per (provider, window) — last 60 min (~60 samples at poller cadence, only appended when `observedAt` changes). `projectedExhaustionAt = now + (100 − current%) / slope`, where slope is the least-squares Δ%/Δt over the buffer. Guards: ≥ 3 distinct samples spanning ≥ 10 min, slope > 0, and projection only shown when it lands **before** `resetsAt` (otherwise the answer is "resets first", which the countdown already conveys). Buffer is memory-only — window *history* is deferred, and losing the buffer on restart merely suppresses the projection for 10 min.
2. **Cost projection (chart):** `rate = windowCostSoFar / minutesElapsed` where elapsed runs from `max(windowStart, first ledger row in window)` to now; dashed line from the now-marker to `windowEnd` at that rate; `projectedCostAtReset = windowCost + rate × minutesRemaining`. Guard: elapsed ≥ 15 min, else null (early-window linear extrapolation is noise — the single most-cited pitfall).
3. Cache-read tokens are excluded from any burn-*health* colouring (they inflate token counts meaninglessly); cost figures need no such exclusion because pi prices buckets correctly upstream.

Rendered sentence on each gauge card, verbatim ccusage-monitor style: *"At the current rate you'll hit 100% at 17:42 — resets 19:00."* / *"On track: resets 19:00 before the limit."*

### D5 — UI: route `/usage`, hand-rolled SVG chart, no new dependency

- **Route:** new TanStack file route `apps/web/src/routes/usage.tsx` with optional search params `{ window?: "primary" | "secondary", provider?: string }`. `SidebarAccountUsagePill`'s `onOpenSettings` becomes `openUsageDashboard` → `navigate({ to: "/usage", search: { provider: view.key } })`. The hover popover stays as-is.
- **Chart library: none.** `apps/web` has no charting dependency today and the requirement is one stacked cumulative step-area with ≤ 168 pre-bucketed points, a now-marker and one dashed line — comfortably a plain-SVG component (`<path>` per model layer, cumulative sums computed in a pure helper). Adding recharts/visx for this contradicts the repo's minimal-surface and performance priorities. Revisit only if the deferred heatmap/history features land.
- **Component tree** (`apps/web/src/components/usage/`):

```
routes/usage.tsx                     — route shell; search-param state; 60 s refetch
  UsageDashboardPage
    WindowToggle                     — 5h ↔ weekly (updates search param)
    WindowGaugeCard (per provider)   — official % bar, countdown, projection sentence, caveat line
    BurnChart                        — plain SVG: stacked cumulative cost, now-marker, dashed projection
      BurnChartLegend                — model → colour swatches
    ModelBreakdownTable              — token buckets × cost × share; header-click sort
    TopConsumersTable                — grouped by rootThreadId, expandable children,
                                       header-click sort, row click → thread route
```

- Pure view maths (bucket → cumulative stack, sort logic, countdown/projection formatting) lives in `packages/client-runtime/src/usageDashboard.ts` next to `accountUsage.ts` — shared with mobile later and unit-testable without the DOM.
- Table sorting is header-click (established preference); consumers default sort = cost desc; thread click-through reuses `threadRoutes.ts` helpers.
- Model colours: stable hash → palette assignment so a model keeps its colour across refetches.

### D6 — Honesty caveats in the UI

- Each gauge card footer: *"Official {provider} figure — counts all clients on this account, not just T3 Code."* (extends the pill's existing wording).
- Breakdown section header chip: *"Tracked by T3 Code only — will not sum to the official meter."*
- Provider column/badge on the model table; models whose provider does not report into the clicked meter's window (e.g. Vertex-served fable/Opus vs the Anthropic OAuth window) get a muted *"not counted in this meter"* badge. v1 keeps this as a static provider-name → meter mapping (Anthropic OAuth ⇢ pi/anthropic instances; Codex ⇢ codex instances; everything else unbadged-but-footnoted); no per-message billing signal exists (`usesSubscriptionPricing` is reserved-but-unset).
- Costs are labelled "API-equivalent cost" — subscription-billed messages carry notional API-rate dollars.
- Trailing-boundary mode banner per D2.

## 4. Implementation plan — 4 coder-sized work packages

**WP1 — Ledger foundations (server + contracts).** Contract fields on `ThreadTokenUsageSnapshot` (`model`, `resolvedModel`, `cacheWriteTokens`); PiDriver stamping at `message_end` + `normalizePiTokenUsage`; migration `046_UsageLedger.ts`; `INSERT OR IGNORE` in `ProviderRuntimeIngestion`. **Boundary:** no query surface, no UI. **Acceptance:** run a live pi turn; a ledger row appears with correct model, four token buckets, and `cost_usd` matching the activity payload; restart the server and confirm no duplicate rows; `vp check` + `vp run typecheck` pass.

**WP2 — Aggregation + RPC (server + client-runtime plumbing).** `AccountUsageRegistry` sample ring buffer + slope helper; window-boundary derivation incl. trailing fallback; `UsageBreakdownQuery` (buckets, models, consumers CTE rollup); `ServerUsageBreakdownInput/Result` + `WsServerGetUsageBreakdownRpc` in contracts; `ws.ts` handler; client-runtime accessor. **Boundary:** consumes WP1's table; no UI. **Acceptance:** RPC returns a well-formed result against a live DB with data in-window; trailing mode exercised by clearing registry state; projection nulls respect the guards.

**WP3 — Dashboard page (web).** Route, pill navigation change, `UsageDashboardPage` with gauges, model table, consumers table, window toggle, caveat copy, 60 s refetch. Burn chart slot renders a placeholder summary (window cost + projected cost). **Boundary:** consumes WP2's RPC; chart visual deferred to WP4. **Acceptance:** pill click lands on `/usage`; tables sort by header click; consumer rows expand and click through to threads; no-data and trailing states render sanely.

**WP4 — Burn chart + projection polish (web).** Plain-SVG stacked cumulative chart with now-marker and dashed projection, legend, gauge projection sentence, `usageDashboard.ts` pure helpers with unit tests where the maths is fiddly (stacking, slope guards). **Boundary:** pure client work on WP3's page. **Acceptance:** chart matches table totals; projection hidden under guard conditions; visual check across both windows.

WP1 → WP2 → WP3 → WP4 strictly ordered; WP3 and WP4 could overlap if staffed separately, but the chart consumes WP3's data wiring so sequential is simpler.

## 5. Risks & open questions

- **Ledger completeness:** only pi emits cost; Codex-driven threads appear token-only (cost 0). Acceptable for v1 — the table shows tokens regardless; flagged in the model table by provider.
- **Anthropic usage endpoint flakiness** (persistent 429s reported upstream): the poller already tolerates failures; stale `observedAt` should mute the projection (guarded by sample-span requirement) — WP2 must treat "stale official data" as "no projection", not extrapolate stale samples.
- **Multiple provider instances of the same driver:** boundaries are per instance; v1 shows all gauges but one breakdown, scoped by clicked provider only for *boundaries*, not filtered rows. If Carl wants per-provider row filtering, it is a one-line WHERE clause later — **open question, human input welcome, default is unfiltered**.
- **`projection_usage_ledger` vs projection rebuilds:** if a projection-rebuild path truncates projection tables, it must either also rebuild the ledger from `orchestration_events` or leave it untouched (it is independently replay-safe). WP1 must check the rebuild path and pick accordingly.
- **Rerouting:** `resolved_model` stays NULL until the ~2-line `pi-vertex-claude` patch lands and is verified live; no UI in v1 renders it.

## 6. Out of scope, restated

No window history persistence, no heatmap, no budget alerts, no subscription-value framing, no subagent attribution, no rerouting UI, no backfill. The schema above accommodates all of the first five without further migration except window history (which would persist the registry sample buffer — a new table when it happens).

# Usage dashboard design — complete

**Deliverable:** implementation-ready design doc at `docs/usage-dashboard-design.md` (signed, role: plan). It unblocks the "Implement usage tracking + dashboard" task, chunked into 4 ordered coder-sized work packages with per-WP acceptance criteria.

Key claims from both research reports were spot-checked against the code and held (snapshot shape, PiDriver `message_end` path, poller→registry→pill chain, activities table, WS RPC pattern).

## Key decisions
- **Data model:** new `projection_usage_ledger` table (migration 046), one row per `thread.token-usage.updated` event, written in `ProviderRuntimeIngestion` with `event_id` PK + `INSERT OR IGNORE` (replay-safe). Rejected `json_extract` over `payload_json` — no index, no historical model data anyway, worse performance. Carries nullable `requested_model`/`resolved_model` from day one (rerouting deferred). **No backfill** — windows roll over within 7 days, so the ledger is complete for all visible windows a week after deploy.
